content:
We need to find a template that when applied to the given molecule (target) reproduces the described forward reaction (carbonyl-ene). We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (integer). We have tools: search_template_catalog_by_criteria, get_template, apply_template, check_smiles_reaction_template_matching, etc. We need to find a template that matches the molecule and corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (break C=O to C-O, break C=C to C-C, form C-C bond, form OH). The description: "ketones and C-C double bonds are gone, while aliphatic hydroxyl and five-membered rings are formed." The molecule given: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: There's an alkene CH2= C attached to aromatic ring (c1... phenyl). Also attached to a chiral carbon (C@@H) that is part of a cyclobutane? Actually [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])... That's a five-membered ring (cyclopentane) with OH on carbon 13, plus CF3 group attached to carbon 15? Wait [C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] is CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13? Actually [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]... So carbon 13 is part of ring and attached to OH and CF3 carbon.

Thus the molecule contains an alkene (CH2= C) and a carbonyl? Actually there is no carbonyl; there is an OH but not carbonyl. The reaction described is carbonyl-ene: a carbonyl (C=O) reacts with an alkene to form new C-C bond and OH. In retrosynthesis, we need to break the C-C bond formed and revert to carbonyl and alkene. So the target molecule is product of carbonyl-ene. So we need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse) will break the C-C bond and generate carbonyl and alkene.

Thus we need to search template catalog for criteria: functional_groups_broken: maybe "ketone" (since forward reaction forms ketone? Actually forward reaction consumes ketone, so in retrosynthesis we break the C-C bond that formed, and we form a ketone. So functional_groups_formed in forward = aliphatic hydroxyl and five-membered ring; broken = ketone and C=C. For retrosynthesis, we want templates that break C-C bond and form C=O and C=C? Wait the tool expects forward reaction criteria. So to find a template for retrosynthesis of carbonyl-ene, we need to specify functional_groups_broken = ["ketone", "C=C"]? Actually forward reaction breaks C=O and C=C (they are consumed) and forms C-O (hydroxyl) and C-C bond. So we set functional_groups_broken = ["ketone", "C=C"] and functional_groups_formed = ["aliphatic_hydroxyl", "five-membered_ring"] maybe. But we need to know exact strings accepted. We can get list via get_available_functional_groups. Let's call that.
